basics.name: Flexure and exact-constraint references: Stuart T. Smith, 'Flexures: Elements of Elastic Mechanisms' (book); Jonathan B. Hopkins' Freedom and Constraint Topologies (FACT, a classification chart and design method); Douglass L. Blanding, 'Exact Constraint: Machine Design Using Kinematic Principles' (book)
basics.url: Smith (publisher page): https://www.routledge.com/Flexures-Elements-of-Elastic-Mechanisms/Smith/p/book/9789056992613 ; Blanding (Google Books record): https://books.google.com/books/about/Exact_Constraint.html?id=DtxSAAAAMAAJ ; FACT overview: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freedom_and_constraint_topologies ; FACT library chart (CC BY-SA): https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Freedom_and_constraint_topologies_(FACT)_library_poster.pdf ; FACT paper (author copy on an MIT course page): https://web.mit.edu/2.70/Reading%20Materials/FACT%20flexure%20design%20Hopkings,%20Culpepper.pdf ; Hopkins' lecture videos: https://www.youtube.com/@TheFACTsofMechanicalDesign/videos ; Hackaday review of Blanding: https://hackaday.com/2019/09/11/books-you-should-read-exact-constraint-machine-design-using-kinematic-principles/
basics.resource_type: book (Smith; Blanding) plus classification system (FACT: a chart of 50 freedom and constraint space 'types', published in peer-reviewed papers, with a free Wikipedia article, a CC-licensed chart and a YouTube lecture channel)
basics.cost: Smith: paid (print and VitalSource eBook from CRC Press/Routledge; price not shown on the page opened) [uncertain]. Blanding: paid (ASME Press hardcover, also listed in the ASME Digital Collection eBooks; price not verified) [uncertain]. FACT: the journal papers are paywalled on ScienceDirect, but an author copy of the 2011 serial-flexure paper is free on an MIT course page; the Wikipedia article, Commons chart and YouTube lectures are free
basics.license: Both books: all rights reserved (link only; do not copy figures). FACT journal papers: (c) Elsevier, all rights reserved. Wikipedia FACT article text: CC BY-SA 4.0. The redrawn FACT library chart on Wikimedia Commons (by Kuba Fober, 2022) is CC BY-SA 4.0, so it can be reused with credit and share-alike
basics.year: Smith: 2000 (CRC Press; Google Books lists 8 Aug 2000, 430 pages; the Routledge page says copyright 2000 and also lists a 444-page format); no later edition found. Blanding: 1999 (ASME Press; Google Books 170 pages, Goodreads 186-page hardcover, first published 1 Oct 1999); no later edition found. FACT: created 2005 by Hopkins as an MIT master's student, first published at ASPE 2006, MS thesis 2007, PhD thesis and 'Part I: Principles' / 'Part II: Practice' papers in Precision Engineering 2010, serial-flexure paper 2011; still taught (ASPE tutorial Nov 2024; YouTube channel active)
basics.access_barrier: paywall for both books and for the FACT journal papers (academic licence via ScienceDirect); none for the Wikipedia article, Commons chart, YouTube lectures, the MIT-hosted author copy and the Hackaday review
basics.image_license: Book figures: all rights reserved. FACT library chart on Commons: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Kuba Fober). The other four FACT figures on the Wikipedia page are Commons files whose licences were not checked [uncertain]. YouTube videos: standard YouTube licence (embed/link only)
basics.authority_level: academic peer-reviewed (FACT papers in Precision Engineering by Hopkins and Culpepper, MIT / LLNL / UCLA) plus professional reference books from established precision-engineering publishers (CRC Press; ASME Press). Blanding's book is widely cited as the classic on exact-constraint design (e.g. quoted in Layton Hale's 1999 MIT thesis chapter used as an MIT course reading)

coverage.covers: Bendy joints (flexures, a kind of compliant mechanism) and how to hold parts so they move only in the wanted directions (exact constraint / kinematic design). Smith covers flexure elements: leaf-type springs, notch hinges, two-axis hinges, the four-bar link, rotationally symmetric hinges (disc coupling, rotationally symmetric leaf hinge, bellows as a flexure), levers, plus elasticity, materials, fatigue, dynamics and machining/heat treatment of flexure materials (about 8 element families in ~430 pages). Blanding covers two-dimensional and three-dimensional connections between objects modelled as constraint lines, constraint devices, flexures (sheet and wire flexures) and couplings, nesting forces and overconstraint (chapter names from a search summary, not an opened contents page [uncertain]). FACT covers every way to arrange wire and blade flexures between rigid bodies for any wanted set of degrees of freedom: a library of 50 freedom/constraint space pairs for parallel flexure systems, extended to serial and hybrid systems and to 'actuation spaces' for placing actuators
coverage.organisation: Smith: textbook order from introduction and elasticity basics, to single flexure elements, to flexure systems, to rotationally symmetric hinges, levers and manufacturing. Blanding: step-by-step from 2D to 3D connections, each chapter ending with a chapter summary, rules collected in an appendix ('Rules for Exact Constraint', seen only as a search-result title) [uncertain]. FACT: a chart laid out in columns by number of degrees of freedom (0 to 6), each column holding numbered types; each cell pairs a freedom space (red rotation lines, black translation arrows) with its complementary constraint space (blue lines). This 'start from the motion you want' order works well for someone who does not know the names, but reading the shapes needs some training
coverage.scope_match: medium: these are the authoritative sources for a family that is squarely in scope (flexure / compliant joints, kinematic mounts, couplings that tolerate misalignment) and FACT is a real classification of flexure arrangements, but they are precision-engineering theory, not a catalogue of named connection types, and they say nothing about fasteners, latches, clutches, gears or adhesives
coverage.taxonomy_used: FACT: 50 'types' of freedom and constraint space pairs (a classification of screw systems suited to flexure design), grouped in 7 columns by degrees of freedom (0-6 DOF), symmetric about the 3-DOF column; a 'parallel pyramid' line separates types reachable by parallel flexures from those needing serial stacking; further split into parallel, serial and hybrid (incl. interconnected hybrid) systems. Blanding: constraint pattern analysis (constraints as lines in space, degrees of freedom as rotation lines; complementary patterns; Maxwell's rule that constraints plus degrees of freedom = 6 for an exactly constrained body). Smith: element vs system, planar vs rotationally symmetric flexures
coverage.example_types: parallel leaf-spring flexure (blade flexure stage); notch hinge (circular/elliptical flexure hinge); cross-strip pivot (crossed-spring pivot); two-axis flexure hinge; four-bar flexure linkage; disc coupling (flexible disc shaft coupling); bellows flexure (bellows coupling); flexure lever (motion reducer/amplifier); wire flexure; sheet flexure; ball-and-socket joint as a 3-constraint connection; gimbal; edge guide with nesting force; lead-screw-to-carriage flexure coupling (FACT 2011 case study); serial flexure stage from stacked parallel modules; Hexblade 6-DOF compliant positioner; bistable binary-stiffness compliant mechanism; zero-stiffness compliant mechanism; compliant rolling-contact mechanism (flexure straps guiding rolling cams)
coverage.making_methods: Precision engineering and instrument design (machined metal flexures, optics mounts, motion stages, MEMS); Blanding's rules apply to any machine and are popular with hobbyist 3D-printer builders (Hackaday); Hopkins' group also uses additive fabrication for flexure-based metamaterials
coverage.item_count: FACT: 50 freedom/constraint space types. Smith: about 8 flexure element/system families in ~430 pages. Blanding: about 5 chapters in ~170-186 pages [uncertain]. Hopkins' YouTube channel: 127 videos
coverage.special_behaviours_covered: compliant: yes, the core subject of all three. Over-centre / bistable: yes in Hopkins' videos (bistable binary-stiffness switch) [uncertain for the books]. Couplings: flexible couplings (disc coupling, bellows) as misalignment-tolerant connections. Preload by nesting force (a spring or gravity holding a part against its locating contacts) is central in Blanding. Actuator placement (FACT actuation spaces), but not powered connectors. Not covered: torque-limiting, self-locking, hand-release only, one-way/ratchet, indexing/detent, print-in-place, gear trains, powered connectors, adhesives
coverage.entry_structure: Book chapters with line diagrams, derivations and worked hardware examples (Blanding adds chapter summaries); FACT chart cells: freedom space + constraint space pair, with rules for choosing flexure elements inside the constraint space and a case study
coverage.audience_level: Smith: advanced undergraduate, graduate and practising engineers (publisher's description). Blanding: professional designers, but readable by hobbyists with little prior knowledge (Hackaday). FACT: graduate/research, with free lecture videos

usefulness.beginner_friendliness: Blanding medium-high (step-by-step, well-diagrammed examples, about 140-170 pages, little prior knowledge assumed, per Hackaday). FACT low-medium (the visual chart is approachable, but it rests on screw theory and projective geometry). Smith low (equation-heavy textbook)
usefulness.has_images: yes: line diagrams throughout the books (not checked in full) [uncertain]; the FACT chart and 5 explanatory figures on Wikipedia are clear colour renderings
usefulness.has_animations: no in the books; yes on Hopkins' YouTube channel 'The FACTs of Mechanical Design' (127 videos: FACT demonstrations, compliant mechanism demos, and a 'Traditional Mechanisms and Mechanical Systems' lecture series)
usefulness.gaps: No plain-English list of connection types; no guidance for 3D-printed flexures (layer direction, PLA/PETG fatigue, print-in-place); no fasteners, snap fits, latches, clutches or adhesives; books are paywalled and their figures cannot be reused; FACT needs screw theory to use beyond looking up the chart
usefulness.good_for_entry_links: Wikipedia FACT article is a stable link for a 'flexure design by degrees of freedom' entry (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freedom_and_constraint_topologies). The books have stable publisher/Google Books pages but no per-type pages; individual YouTube videos can be linked from specific compliant-mechanism entries
usefulness.reusable_data: FACT chart: CC BY-SA 4.0 on Commons, reusable with credit and share-alike; the list of 50 types can be rebuilt from the papers (facts are not copyrightable) but no dataset exists. Books: not reusable
usefulness.maintained: Books: static (no new editions found since 1999/2000; Smith is still sold as print and eBook). FACT: actively taught and extended (UCLA Flexible Research Group research page, ASPE tutorial 4-5 Nov 2024, YouTube channel)
usefulness.ideas_to_borrow: (1) Start the flow chart from the motion you want ('which directions should it move or turn?'), as FACT does, then show the matching joint layouts. (2) Blanding's simple counting rule in plain words: every direction you block is one constraint; blocking a direction twice makes it bind or wobble (overconstraint), so 6 minus the number of free motions = number of constraints needed. (3) 'Nesting force': say what holds the part against its locating points. (4) Hopkins' build-your-own flexure kits and short demo videos as hands-on learning. (5) Group flexures by element (blade, wire, notch hinge, cross-strip pivot, bellows, disc) like Smith
usefulness.design_rules_given: Smith: yes, analytic stiffness and stress formulas for leaf springs, notch hinges and other elements, fatigue and material data, machining and heat-treatment notes [uncertain for exact tables]. Blanding: qualitative rules (constraint counting, complementary patterns, nesting forces) rather than numbers. FACT: rules for placing constraints, no dimensions
usefulness.generator_or_parametric: None found: no CAD generator or parametric models; FACT is a paper/chart method (the Commons chart is a redrawn PDF/JPG)
usefulness.file_formats: Print books and eBook (VitalSource for Smith); PDF journal papers; Commons chart as PDF and JPG; YouTube video
usefulness.terminology_value: high for flexure and constraint terms: degree of freedom, constraint line, overconstraint/underconstraint, exact constraint, kinematic design, nesting force, notch hinge, cross-strip pivot, blade/wire/sheet flexure, freedom space, constraint space, twist, wrench. No translations
usefulness.decision_support: FACT works as a lookup selector: pick the wanted degrees of freedom, find that freedom space in the chart, read off its constraint space, then place flexures inside it (with Maxwell's rule to check). Blanding's constraint pattern analysis is a manual check method. No interactive tool or filters
usefulness.derived_from_or_overlaps: Exact-constraint/kinematic design goes back to Maxwell (1890) and instrument makers; FACT builds on exact-constraint design and screw theory, and a FACT chapter appears in the Handbook of Compliant Mechanisms (Wiley 2013, pp. 79-92, per Wikipedia), overlapping the BYU Compliant Mechanisms item. Layton Hale's 1999 MIT thesis chapter on exact-constraint design (an MIT OCW 2.76 reading, https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/2-76-multi-scale-system-design-fall-2004/3aa5862a1724b75c3e4aa7a6fee6c511_reading_l3.pdf) quotes Blanding and overlaps the Slocum FUNdaMENTALs item. Roth's Konstruktionskataloge Band 2 has a parallel German treatment of blocking motion with support points (Stuetzpunkte)
